Analysis conditions

Default auto-analysis uses paged-evidence-v2. The optional public-given-entrypoints-v1 condition initializes anonymous function entries from the task's supplied RVAs and public ELF load mappings, making those supplied caller/callee boundaries available to function queries. Localization remains unseeded. The original binaries, public packages and earlier attempts are preserved. These analysis conditions remain separate in the capability summaries.

Conditions ending in .role-string-v1 additionally deliver an explicit public serialization rule: each record-field role is one identifier string, while supplied semantic paths are arrays. The exact notice is a prompt input bound by the inference action. Earlier cached submissions retain their original condition and grade.

Incomplete budget-exhausted attempts retain their observed tokens and estimated costs and remain ungraded. Complete final answers that cross a threshold retain their correctness grade separately from the budget exceeded / attempt stopped label. A correctly bound budget-stop receipt can verify request enforcement independently of task success. Strict runtime certification still requires its completion evidence; saved pre/post checks alone do not retroactively create a missing completion manifest.

Capability vectors and family macros

Metrics stay separate: L1 uses top-1 success, L2–L4 use F1, L5 uses full-chain success with component diagnostics, and C/T use their capability check fraction. No applicable semantic fact yields no metric observation, rather than free credit. Variants average within a family; related families average within a declared lineage; lineages receive equal weight. All current integer-record ABI forms share one lineage. Recovery and full-semantics generation conditions are separate rows. Premises-only controls remain in saved history and expenditure, separate from recovery macros. An observed-subset macro is descriptive; a full-denominator macro requires every scheduled cell to have a grade. Shared-case macros use the same graded public packages across selected models.

Immutable pre-run registration

New capability dispatch requires an immutable schedule and a complete execution binding before any selected queue starts. The schedule fixes selection, budgets, metric definitions, family weights and parallelism. The binding fixes original builds, grading contracts and every prospective runtime/provider route. Unsupported caps fail before runtime inventory. A single-use dispatch intent links each new task to those records. Cached observations keep their original provenance; offline reuse creates no new experiment. Registration is local admission evidence, not a remote signature or model-weight attestation.
